publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: The discount factor for reinforcement learning has been constrained to the range [0, 1] to avoid overestimation of state values during training. Although theoretical studies have indicated that discount factors greater than 1 could be valid for certain tasks, experimental work has generally maintained the [0, 1] limit in flexible discount factor optimization. Our study explores the impact of allowing discount factors to exceed 1 across a variety of reinforcement learning algorithms and classic training environments. Our findings demonstrate that in some grid-based environments, reinforcement learning algorithms with discount factors above 1 can achieve comparable performance to those with discount factors within the [0, 1] range. However, performance tends to be more variable when the discount factor exceeds 1.

articleTitle: Research on Surface Flow Velocity Measurements Based on Ground-Based Synthetic Aperture Radar Configurations
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: This study introduces a novel approach for measuring water surface flow velocity using a Ground-Based Synthetic Aperture Radar (GB-SAR) configuration. Addressing the limitations of long revisit periods and high costs associated with satellite-based and airborne Along-Track Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (ATI-SAR) observations, the proposed method involves deploying two GB-SARs on the ground scene to capture consecutive images of the same water body in a short time frame. By analyzing the phase difference between these images, specifically the Along-Track Interferometric, the water surface flow velocity can be accurately determined. Simulation results demonstrate the efficacy of this method.

articleTitle: Tensor Extreme Learning Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In recent years, with the advancement of deep learning network, the classification performance of hyperspectral image (HSI) has been continuously improved. Deep learning is capable of extracting spatial features from hyperspectral data. Nonetheless, it encounters two primary challenges in hyperspectral image processing. Firstly, a substantial number of labeled samples are needed for training, yet acquiring them is both expensive and time-consuming; secondly, the large-scale models in deep learning lead to excessively long training times. Therefore, how to implement fast and accurate HSI classification with a small number of labeled samples has become a current research focus. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a method called tensor extreme learning network (TELN). This method utilizes tensor theory to rapidly extract deep spatial features from hyperspectral data, with fast training speed. Comparative experiments show that the proposed TELN is better than deep learning method both in time efficiency and accuracy.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of the Integration of Satellite and Terrestrial Networks Under UAV Interference
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In the spectrum-sharing space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs), the system capacity can be improved by spectrum sharing. However, co-channel interference is unavoidable due to the shared spectrum, which may increase the system outage probability and bit error rate (BER). In this paper, the problem of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) interference with terrestrial users in the integration of satellite and terrestrial networks (ISTNs) is investigated. For measuring the interference performance from UAV to terrestrial users, the Quasi Deterministic Radio Channel Generator (QuaDRiGa) channel simulator is introduced to establish the link-level simulation experiment platform based on MATLAB for the ISTN. On this basis, the outage probability is derived when the satellite-terrestrial channel is modeled as Shadowed-Rician (SR) distribution and the terrestrial interference channel is modeled as Nakagami-m distribution. Furthermore, the bit error rate (BER) of the system is derived for Barrage Noise Interference (BNI) and Partial band Interference (PBI) of the UAV respectively. Finally, the simulation experiment results show that within the main lobe region of the receiving antenna, interference generated by UAVs leads to a significant increase in system outage probability and a significant decrease in BER performance.

articleTitle: Design of a Miniaturized Dual Notch UWB-MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: A miniaturized dual notch ultra-wideband multiple-iput multiple (UWB-MIMO) antenna is proposed in this paper. Rectangular patches and microstrip lines are cut and grooved to achieve good ultra-wideband characteristics. By cutting and grooving on both sides of the ground floor and adding a fork-type decoupling structure in the middle, the coupling of the antenna is reduced, so as to achieve high isolation. “L” grooves and inverted “U” grooves are etched on the radiation patch to realize the notch in the WLAN partial frequency band (5.47 ~ 5.725 GHz) and the X-band downlink frequency band (7.25 ~ 7.75 GHz). The antenna isolation is less than-18dB,the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) remains below 0.003, and the overall performance is superior. It can be widely used in various ultra-wideband communication systems.

articleTitle: Design of Batch Folder Secret Level Labeling Software Based on Python
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: The secret level of folders has always been a problem that is easily overlooked in the process of file secret labeling, leading to violations of confidentiality regulations. This article analyzes the confidentiality regulations for files and folders of administration institutions and confidential agencies, and develops a batch folder secret level program using Python and commonly used Python libraries. This program can correctly label the secret levels of all folders and subfolders on a directory tree, and can decompress and label compressed packages correctly, having solved the problem of unprocessed folders in traditional batch file secret level labeling software. Tests have shown that it can achieve good results.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Objective Optimized Server Deployment Strategy in Edge Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In edge computing environments, reasonable edge server placement is one of the key issues, which directly affects user access latency and server resource utilisation. Aiming at the inefficiency and poor performance of existing placement methods, this study proposes an edge server placement method (KG-ESP) based on an improved heuristic algorithm. The method optimises the k-means algorithm, reduces randomness by adjusting the selection of initial clustering centres, and improves the convergence speed and stability of the algorithm. At the same time, it combines the greedy algorithm to load-balance the servers. By comparing with the three baseline methods, the simulation experiment results show that the KG-ESP method effectively reduces the access latency and improves the resource utilisation efficiency, indicating that the application of this method in edge computing scenarios has obvious advantages.

articleTitle: A Finetuned Multimodal Deep Learning Model for Xray Image Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Generative conversational AI has shown significant potential in aiding biomedical professionals, yet existing research predominantly targets single-mode textual communication. While multimodal conversational AI has advanced quickly through utilizing vast numbers of image-text pairs available online, these broad-domain vision-language models are still insufficiently refined in their ability to comprehend and discuss biomedical imagery. This article primarily addresses question-answering (QA) for medical imaging data and cancer diagnosis. We constructed a relevant instruction-based QA dataset and performed directive fine-tuning on the Qwen-VL 7B model. Thanks to the use of QLora technology, our model can be trained quickly on a Nvidia RTX 4090 graphics card and achieves better results compared to other multimodal models. The experiments showed that the Qwen- VL-7B model has best Rouge-1, Rouge-2, Rouge-L score compared to other models, meaning its highly potential for medical question-answering application.

articleTitle: Improved Intersection Multi-Source Sensing Fusion Method of YOLOX
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In the intersection scene, millimeter wave radar has poor perception effect on static target, and its visual perception has the problem of missing detection of small target. In order to solve these problems, the convolutional attention mechanism is introduced in this paper, and VariFocal loss and CIoU loss are used to optimize the loss function of YOLOX to improve the detection performance of small targets. To solve the problem of static target missing detection, the sensor fusion algorithm of millimeter wave radar and camera based on double similarity index is designed, and the sensor fusion accuracy is improved by the target state correction method. Finally, the algorithm is transplanted to the roadside edge computing equipment, and the test data is collected and analyzed under different weather conditions. The results show that the accuracy of perception fusion algorithm can reach 91.33% in sunny, cloudy and night scenarios.

articleTitle: A Module of Fiber Optic Communication for High-Temperature Downhole Environments in Oil Wells
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Compared to traditional downhole transmission methods, fiber optic communication enables real-time, high data rate transmission. However, the foremost challenge that downhole optical communication faces is how to ensure prolonged operation in the harsh environment, characterized by high temperatures, high pressures, and corrosive substances. This paper introduces the system structure and design scheme of optical fiber communication in oil well in detail. Based on high temperature optoelectronic devices and chips, this paper develops a novel high-temperature-resistant downhole communication module. Without the need for thermal insulation, this module enables prolonged, real-time, bidirectional, high-speed communication between downhole instruments and surface equipment. The system performance specifications include withstanding temperatures up to 150 °C, achieving a communication rate of 10Mbps, and supporting communication distances greater than 8 km.

articleTitle: Passive Isolator Based on Electromagnetically Induced Transparent Coupling Resonance in Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Non-reciprocal optical devices in integrated systems on a chip have attracted great interest due to the increasing demand for researching integrated photonics and silicon photonics. The non-reciprocal devices include optical isolators, circulators, and optical amplifiers. In this paper, We analyze the dynamic nonreciprocity of an optical isolator based on the principle of electromagnetically induced transparency, and show a comparison of the nonreciprocal transmission when waves are transmitted forward and backward. The results show that when energy is transmitted, this isolator can realize signal isolation with specific direction transmission at non-single frequency. This device can be used in a wide range of signal processing and optical communication applications.

articleTitle: W-Band Sine Waveguide TWT Based Upon Power Combining of Four
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: A four-way power combiner employing a flat-roofed sine waveguide (FRSWG) slow wave structure (SWS) has been proposed to enhance the output power of W-band traveling wave tubes (TWTs). This approach leverages power combiner technology to achieve higher power levels. The design incorporates a T-shaped waveguide to create a 1:4 power divider, which is then utilized as the input/output structure for the entire system. In this configuration, the four TWTs operate independently and their outputs are combined by the power combiner. High-frequency software simulations indicate that the transmission S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>exceeds -1 dB, while the reflection S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>is less than -15 dB. Operating with a voltage of 19 kV, a current of 200 mA, and an input power of 1.2 W, the entire structure can produce an output power of 450 W with a gain of 25.7 dB. Particle-in-cell simulations confirm that across the frequency band of 90–100 GHz, the power output can reach 360 W with a gain exceeding 25 dB.

articleTitle: Measurement-Based Improved Two-Ray Model for Maritime Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: The ocean covers 71% of the global surface, making the study of maritime communication critical for achieving global coverage in 6G communications. Large-scale path loss characteristics play a pivotal role in the study of communication coverage. In this paper, we conduct channel detection experiments for sea-to-sea and sea-to-shore communications at 3.2GHz and propose an improved two-ray path loss model. The model accounts for the effects of seawater electrolytes on electromagnetic wave propagation and fully considers the rough reflections caused by sea surface fluctuations. Utilizing the Fresnel zone, we define the applicability of the two-ray model. The paper focuses on the influence of sea surface reflection, modeling the reflection path's coefficient as the product of the specular reflection coefficient and sea surface smoothness. Considering factors such as antenna height, distance, temperature and salinity, we derive the specular reflection coefficient using the Debye model and represent the rough reflection with the Rayleigh parameter. The good fit between the measured channel data and the two-ray model demonstrates that the proposed model effectively characterizes path loss in maritime environments.

articleTitle: Defect Pattern Classification of Wafer Graph based on Dual Channel Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: For the issue of wafer defect classification in semiconductor manufacturing, we propose a lightweight method for nonhomologous two-channel feature extraction method based on a convolutional neural network (CNN), employing CNNA and CNNB channels. In both channels, we replace the traditional fully connected layer with a global average pooling layer, thereby reducing parameter computation. Initially, addressing the imbalance in wafer defect categories using oversampling and standardize image size through nearest neighbor interpolation. Subsequently, to comprehensively capture wafer image features, CNNA employs larger filter sizes while CNNB utilizes smaller ones, supplemented with zero padding. Finally, we fuse the feature vectors from both channels for classification. The method is validated on the WM-811K dataset, achieving a classification accuracy of 75% without denoising. Comparison with other models highlights the superiority of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Lead-Level ECG Signal Quality Assessment Based on Weak Supervision and Multi-Branch Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: 12-lead Electrocardiogram (ECG) is a common test for diagnosis of cardiovascular disease and each ECG lead reflects the heart activities from different aspects. Due to the environmental noise interference in daily life, the assessment of ECG signal quality is of great importance for accurate diagnosis. However, due to the lack of lead-level quality labels, existing methods only perform coarser record-level quality assessment, which may reject lead of good quality or accept poor-quality lead. To overcome this limitation, the paper proposes a multi-branch fusion model for lead-level quality assessment under weak supervision. In this framework, each lead corresponds to a multi-scale convolutional network which produces a lead-level score, and a dense gating network assigns a weight value to each individual lead. The record-level quality score of the multi-lead ECG signals is obtained by aggregating the lead-level quality scores. The proposed method was evaluated on the PhysioNet/CinC2011 dataset and achieved an accuracy of 95.5%, a sensitivity of 98.07%, and an F1 score of 97.13%. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively assess the quality of 12-lead ECG signal at both record and lead levels.

articleTitle: Chinese Fraudulent Text Message Detection Based on Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of mobile phones, the frequency of criminals exploiting text messages for scams is on the rise. However, due to the sparse and deceptive nature of Chinese text messages, existing detection methods struggle to effectively combat this issue. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel network model leveraging graph neural networks. Initially, we utilize BERT as a word embedding tool to derive word vectors from the text. Subsequently, we construct a word-document heterogeneous graph based on these word vectors. Then, employing Graph Attention Networks (GAT), we learn features between the nodes of the graph. Finally, we integrate the predictions from BERT and GAT to form the final prediction result. Experimental results on two publicly available datasets demonstrate that our proposed model outperforms other state-of-the-art models in performance.

articleTitle: Research on SQL Injection Detection Method Based on Mixed Word Embedding
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: With the rapid development of the internet, the challenges of network security are becoming increasingly severe. SQL injection attacks are one of the primary security threats faced by web applications today. Characterized by their diverse types, rapid evolution, covert attack methods, and significant damage, the number of SQL injection attacks is on the rise year by year. Currently, mainstream SQL injection detection methods are mostly based on traditional machine learning and deep learning algorithms, which have issues such as imperfect word vector training methods and insufficient classification accuracy. Therefore, this paper proposes an AWTextCNN model based on a hybrid word embedding method. This model employs the Albert-Word2vec hybrid word embedding method for word vector training and uses the TextCNN model for classification. Experimental results show that the AWTextCNN model achieves an accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score of 99.73%, 99.75%, 99.66%, and 99.70<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> respectively on the test set, demonstrating excellent performance in the field of SQL injection detection.

articleTitle: Heavy Overload Transformer Oil Temperature Prediction Method Based on Multivariate Spatio-Temporal Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: The top layer oil temperature of a transformer under heavy overload conditions can change rapidly, which affects the insulation performance of the transformer and shortens its operational life. Therefore, the prediction of top layer oil temperature can provide an important basis for early warning of transformer failure. However, single oil temperature data cannot accurately reflect the oil temperature change rule, and the multivariate oil temperature spatio-temporal features are difficult to capture. In order to solve the existing problems, this paper proposes a new heavy overload transformer oil temperature prediction method based on multivariate spatio-temporal convolutional network (MSTCN). The top oil temperature, environmental temperature and load data are first normalized. Then the dataset is inputted into MSTCN to explore the temporal information through gated recurrent unit, utilized the dimensionality-enhanced channel attention mechanism to focus on more important variables and detailed features, and took the convolutional and self-attention mechanism to mine the spatial information. Finally, the prediction results are output through fully connected layers and denormalization. The method is compared with the advanced techniques, and the effectiveness and advancement of the method is proved through experiments.

articleTitle: Cluster-Based Load Balancing in Millimeter-Wave Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Millimeter wave (mmWave) has become the main working frequency band in 5G and 6G communication networks due to its high bandwidth, large capacity, and low latency characteristics, but it provides users with high-quality data rates and is also subject to the constraints of penetration capability and coverage. Therefore, mmWave networks are more densely deployed with small base stations (SBSs), which creates a huge impact on user scheduling and load balancing (LB) in the network. In this paper, we propose a LB strategy based on clustered mmWave networks, which aims at balancing the load between mmWave SBSs and improving the quality of service (QoS) for users in the network at the same time. Simulations show that our proposed scheme not only guarantees better user sum data rates, but also has higher stability compared to baseline.

articleTitle: A UAV Sensor Fault Detection Model Based on Dual-Threshold Method and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: With the popularization and application of drone technology in many industries, ensuring the safety of drone flights and detecting drone faults has become an important challenge. Sensors are an important part of UAV flight safety. Ensuring the normal operation of sensors is crucial to ensure UAV flight safety. However, due to the risk of sensor loss or failure when UAVs perform extreme missions, UAVs pose significant challenges to flight safety and mission completion. This study proposes a UAV sensor failure analysis method that combines a dual-threshold model and a data-driven deep neural network. The method employs a long short-term memory (LSTM) network for sensor fault prediction. This method combines the advantages of a fast and direct fixed model with strong plasticity of a data-driven model, achieving good performance. The study conducted experimental verification using the BASiC data set. The results demonstrate that this method exhibits high adaptability and high accuracy in UAV sensor fault detection, thereby providing a high-precision UAV sensor fault judgment method for the future.

articleTitle: Application of Re-Configurable Intelligence Surfaces (RIS) in Cross-Protocol and Multi-Link Communications System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Electromagnetic meta-materials and meta-surfaces are hot-spots in the fields of information and materials, which brings a new technical direction to the radio wave propagation for the future wireless communication system. Re-configurable Intelligence Surfaces(abbreviated as RIS) can manipulate electromagnetic waves by digital coding, which provide the technical operability of cross-protocol and multi-link hybrid communication. The structure design and array electronic layout of the reflector unit of RIS play an important role in the adjustment of multi-band electromagnetic beams. By encoding the meta-surface characterization parameters in space and time domains, the energy radiation of electromagnetic wave and information modulation are integrated together.

articleTitle: Hardware Design of Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control Based on Floating-Point Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control (LADRC) has been widely employed in automatic control due to its enhanced robustness and superior anti-interference capability. However, most current LADRC applications are based on the software level, which exhibits a relatively low response speed compared to the hardware implementation and does not apply to specific scenarios requiring high response speed. This paper presents a hardware design of LADRC based on a single-precision floating point, which guarantees arithmetic precision and a high response speed. The feasibility of this hardware implementation is demonstrated by applying it in a fully integrated digitally controlled BOOST circuit under a 180 nm process. The proposed LADRC in this paper shows a 20% improvement in response speed in BOOST circuits while maintaining stability ripple at 0.9% of the target output with a maximum error of 0.6%.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Backoff Algorithm Based on Topology Status for Flying Ad hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In recent years, the utilization of flying ad hoc networks (FANETs) has seen a gradual rise across diverse civilian and military applications. The high mobility of nodes in FANETs leads to highly dynamic topology, frequent disruptions in links, and heightened competition for channel access. Traditional adaptive backoff algorithms primarily adjust the backoff window based on wireless channel states, achieving only local network optimality and restraining network performance. This paper first proposes a network global backoff window optimization algorithm T-BEB based on global network topology status, and conducts algorithm performance analysis through BOBYQA. On this basis, this paper implements the algorithm through the link state routing protocol (NLSR) in the named data network (NDN) in ns-3, and simulates the network performance under different loads and node mobility. It is verified that when network traffic is saturated and nodes have high mobility, compared with the traditional BEB algorithm, the T-BEB algorithm can reduce packet delay and system packet loss rate, and improve system throughput.

articleTitle: Low Illumination Image Enhancement Algorithm Based on Illumination Equalization and Edge Detail Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In order to ensure the safe and efficient operation of the railway, the railway foreign object intrusion monitoring system has become the main way to obtain information. Due to the low visibility of the images collected at night in the low illumination environment, the loss of detail information is serious, which seriously reduces the accuracy of video intelligent recognition. To solve these problems, this paper proposes an image enhancement algorithm based on illumination equalization and edge detail enhancement. Firstly, the S component and V component of the image in the color space HSV are stretched, and the adaptive bilateral filter function is used as the center surrounding function to extract the light component of the low illumination image. Then, the two-dimensional gamma function is used to correct the image brightness to obtain the illumination balanced image; Then the four direction Sobel operator is used to extract the edge details of the image, and the image depicting the edge details is obtained; Finally, the enhanced image is obtained by multi weight feature pyramid image fusion. The method proposed in this paper is tested by selecting the video images in the low illumination environment at night in the railway integrated monitoring system. The experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper is superior to other classical algorithms in terms of SSIM, PSNR, NIQE evaluation indicators. The algorithm in this paper can effectively improve the brightness and clarity of low illumination images at night, while making the enhanced image contain more image edge details.

articleTitle: A Semantic Communication System Based on Vector Quantization and Generative Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Most existing semantic communication systems directly map source data to channel symbols, resulting in constellation points that may appear at arbitrary positions within the constellation, which is somewhat inconsistent with contemporary digital communication system design. In this paper, we propose a high-performance deep learning-based quantized vector (VQ) semantic communication (SC) system, named VQ-DeepSC-E, where only limited indices need to be transmitted at the transmitter to reconstruct images at the receiver, significantly reducing communication costs and aligning more closely with digital communication systems. Compared to existing VQ semantic communication systems, the proposed method utilizes generative adversarial network (GAN) to extract image features, enhances feature indexing performance and reduces the generation of artifacts in reconstructed images. The simulation results indicate that the proposed method achieves superior Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) and Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS) scores compared to the existing VQ-DeepSC method.

articleTitle: Precoding Optimization Algorithm for Visible Light Communication Based on Lattice Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: To tackle the issue of strong spatial correlation among sub-channels caused by the implementation of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology in indoor visible light communication (VLC) systems, which consequently leads to inter-channel interference, a comprehensive solution is proposed. This solution aims to jointly enhance channel transmission quality by seamlessly integrating the lattice reduction algorithm with the minimum mean square error (MMSE) algorithm. Through the application of lattice reduction, the channel matrix is transformed into an equivalent form with significantly improved orthogonality. Additionally, the utilization of the MMSE criterion effectively reduces spatial correlation within the MIMO channel, resulting in superior bit error rate (BER) performance compared to the traditional MMSE precoding approach. Simulation results reveal that this scheme effectively mitigates spatial correlation within the channel. Notably, the BER performance of a 2×2 system surpasses that of a 4×4 system. Specifically, for the 4×4 system, when the BER attains a level of 10–3, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is reduced by approximately 3 dB in comparison to the conventional MMSE precoding technique.

articleTitle: A Long Distance Environmental Monitoring System Based on Low Power IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: This article proposes a remote environmental monitoring system based on low-power Internet of Things, which is applied in smart agriculture to achieve remote and real-time measurement of temperature, humidity, and light intensity parameters in the crop growth environment within the coverage range of the device The system adopts low-power Internet of Things technology, which has the characteristics of wide coverage, multiple connections, fast speed, low cost, low power consumption, and excellent architecture. The overall design of the system includes multiple environmental monitoring nodes, a LoRa gateway, and corresponding environmental monitoring upper computer software. In terms of system software, it involves programming of node MCU and client upper computer software. The key technology implementation includes the hardware design and implementation of low-power sensor nodes and the development of LoRa protocol. System testing and performance analysis show that the optimized LoRa protocol performs well in communication distance, power consumption, stability, and other aspects, laying the foundation for the efficient operation of the system. This study provides a powerful tool for sustainable resource management, which helps to promote agricultural modernization and rural revitalization.

articleTitle: Pioneering ESG Evaluation: A Cloud-Based Framework Leveraging Machine Learning and Domain-Driven Design
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In response to the growing demand for robust ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) evaluation frameworks, this paper presents a pioneering approach that integrates machine learning techniques, cloud computing, and Domain-Driven Design (DDD) principles. The proposed framework offers a comprehensive solution for evaluating the ESG performance of organizations, leveraging ML models to analyze vast datasets and extract valuable insights. By adopting DDD principles, the framework ensures the alignment of technical solutions with domain-specific requirements, enhancing its effectiveness and usability. Through empirical validation using public data, the efficacy and reliability of the framework are demonstrated, underscoring its potential to drive sustainable decision-making and corporate governance practices.

articleTitle: Two-Way Authentication Scheme for Railway Time Synchronization Protocol Based on Hybrid Key Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of missing client authentication in the NTP protocol of railroad time synchronization network, we propose a two-way authentication scheme based on hybrid key enhancement. The scheme securely transmits the public key based on the cryptography of the identity and securely negotiates a temporary key by asymmetric encryption. At the same time, we utilize the host's current time as a sequence number to defend against replay attacks. Two-way authentication is accomplished through the identity checksum generated from the temporary key and the sequence number. Subsequently, we use the temporary key encryption to protect the subsequent message transmission. This scheme not only reduces the lack of client authentication, but also provides forward and backward security. Finally, we formally verified the scheme using the proverif tool. The validation results show that our method outperforms other methods in terms of security and authentication overhead, and is able to satisfy the security and real-time requirements of bidirectional authentication for NTP protocols.

articleTitle: Research on Steel Surface Defect Detection Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In response to the issues of missed detections, false alarms, low detection accuracy, high computational complexity, and large model parameters in the current YOLOv8 algorithm for steel surface defect detection, this paper introduces the lightweight VanillaNet network and CBAM attention mechanism to improve detection performance on small targets, enhance model detection accuracy, and reduce model complexity further by introducing the AKConv module, proposing an improved YOLOv8 algorithm. In this study, we focus on using the NEU-DET dataset and conduct extensive experiments using the PyTorch framework to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm. The experimental results show that the improved detection algorithm has a parameter count and computational complexity of 1.72M and 5.0GFLOPS, respectively, reducing by 45% and 43.8% compared to the original YOLOv8, with an average accuracy of 84.3%, which is 3.2% higher than the original YOLOv8.

articleTitle: Comparison of HDD and SSD Read/Write Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Hard drives include hard Disk drives (HDD) and Solid State drives (SSD). In general, the read/write speed of SSD is much faster than that of traditional HDD. The read speed of SSD can generally reach 400M/s. The read/write speed of an SSD is 3–5 times that of HDD [1]. This means that applications can be loaded, files are read, and data is transferred faster when using SSDS. The performance of the device is higher. Under different data block sizes, the read/write speeds of SSDS and HDDS are different. This paper focuses on the study of the difference in read/write speeds of 24 SSDS and HDDS in 12 service scenarios. It is found that the read/write performance advantage of SSDS with small data blocks is greater than that of large data blocks, especially in the scenario where the data block is 8K and the read/write ratio is 80%.

articleTitle: Significant Target-Guided Feature Extraction Algorithm Based on Optimized Superpoint
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In order to address the problems of low efficiency and poor accuracy of feature extraction in the process of heterogeneous image alignment caused by the complex environment of the substation and the heat interference of various power equipment. This paper proposes a significant target-guided feature extraction algorithm optimizing SuperPoint based on the SuperPoint algorithm. Firstly, based on the original SuperPoint algorithm framework, an image preprocessing link is added, edge features are extracted using the Canny algorithm, and the extracted edge features are fused with the original to strengthen the contour information of the image. Secondly, a significant target-guided feature extraction strategy is proposed, which uses the K-means image segmentation algorithm to mark the significant target region in the image and the process of feature extraction, the feature extraction is mainly carried out on the significant target region, to reduce the percentage of the number of feature points in the background, and to improve the efficiency of feature extraction and accuracy. The experimental results show that the feature extraction algorithm proposed in this paper has higher accuracy and robustness. On the CAO-C2F dataset, the alignment rate of this algorithm after feature extraction is 87.31%, and the time consumed is 112.58ms, which is 12.04% higher than the original SuperPoint algorithm and 23.09ms lower than the original SuperPoint algorithm, which proves that the algorithm proposed in this paper is superior for the feature extraction in the process of alignment of heterogeneous images of substation equipment.

articleTitle: Evaluations of Multi-Step Traffic Flow Prediction Models Based on Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Accurate prediction of traffic flow is crucial for alleviating traffic congestion, optimizing resource allocation and enhancing the efficiency of transport systems. In recent years, graph neural networks (GNNs) have been widely used in the field of traffic flow prediction due to their advantages in processing graph-structured data. This study provides an in-depth comparative analysis of the performance of several representative GNN models in a multi-step traffic flow prediction task. Through a unified training system, the experiments on real-world traffic flow datasets (PEMS 04 and 08) reveal the performance differences of five typical models: STGCN, DCRNN, GWNET, AGCRN and MTGNN. The results show that although the compared five models all exhibit excellent performance compared to traditional methods (HA, ARIMA and LSTM), there are significant differences in their efficiencies under specific conditions. The speed of STGCN, AGCRN and MTGNN are much faster than that of DCRNN and GWNET. Finally, how to further improve these models is also discussed with the consideration of node-specific prediction tasks.

articleTitle: Design Study of a New Portable Thermal Anemometer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: The objective of this study is to develop a new portable thermal anemometer that is cost-effective, highly accurate, offers a wide measurement range, and is handheld. Utilizing Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), this research designs a portable anemometer housing equipped with an innovative shunt structure. It further analyzes the influence of key structural parameters of the sampling flow channel—namely, the length of the flat section, the diameter of the round tube, and the cross-section ratio—on the device's performance. A control circuit is then tailored according to system requirements, and the final assembly of the anemometer is accomplished using 3D printing and PCB technologies. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that this anemometer substantially reduces the wind speed across the surface of the flow sensor chip while maintaining laminar flow conditions throughout the test range, thereby significantly expanding the test range.

articleTitle: An Online Anomaly Detection Algorithm with Adaptive Concept Drift
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In response to the existing offline anomaly detection algorithms performing well on static data, but struggle to meet the requirements of accuracy and real-time processing when the data distribution changes. This paper proposes an online anomaly detection algorithm with concept drift adaptation to adapt to continuously changing data distributions. Firstly, the data is subjected to offline training using a Long Short-Term Memory autoencoder to obtain anomaly scores. And unsupervised anomaly detection is performed based on dynamic thresholds. Then, an adaptive sliding window is employed for concept drift detection, with the model being updated and adjusted through concept drift adaptation. Finally, the improved Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm is utilized to optimize the hyperparameters that contribute more to the accuracy. Results indicate that the proposed algorithm effectively adapts to evolving data distributions, meeting the real-time processing and accuracy requirements essential for anomaly detection.

articleTitle: Comparison and Analysis of DC-Biased OFDM Channel Estimation Algorithms in VLC Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: With the rapid development of wireless communication technology, visible light communication (VLC) systems have attracted increasing interest from researchers and are gradually moving towards industrialization due to their ability to provide both low-power indoor lighting and high-speed wireless access. DC-Biased optical OFDM (DCO-OFDM) has been proposed for VLC systems to provide optically power efficient solution and easy implementation. In this work, comb type pilot arrangement and block type pilot arrangement are proposed for the DCO-OFDM systems over visible light channels. In this paper, Least Squares (LS) algorithm, Linear Minimum Mean Square Error (LMMSE) algorithm and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) algorithm are used to compare the bit error rate (BER) performance of comb pilot insertion and block pilot insertion in DCO-OFDM system under visible light channel. Furthermore, three interpolation algorithms tailored for comb pilot insertion are specifically introduced. This paper has certain reference value for channel estimation algorithm and pilot selection.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-Based Client Selection for Enhanced Model Convergence in Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Federated learning enables the collaborative training of a global model while allowing the data of multiple clients to remain local. This characteristic renders federated learning highly sensitive to the quality of client data, computational performance, and network conditions. In real-world scenarios, there can be significant disparities in data quality, computational capabilities, and network conditions among clients. Such heterogeneity can severely impact the convergence speed and quality of the global model. To address these challenges, we propose a client selection algorithm that comprehensively considers various metrics of clients. Utilizing fuzzy reasoning, this algorithm analyzes and evaluates clients, enabling the server to select those most conducive to federated training. Extensive experiments conducted across multiple datasets demonstrate that, compared to other client selection algorithms, our algorithm not only marginally improves the accuracy of the global model but also significantly enhances its convergence speed.

articleTitle: Efficient Feature Selection Algorithm Based on Counterfactuals
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Feature selection is crucial for model construction, involving the identification and selection of the most predictive subset of features from the original set. While information theory-based feature selection algorithms are broadly utilized, they primarily assess correlations and fail to uncover causality, which is essential for pinpointing key decision-influencing features. Additionally, the computational efficiency of these algorithms is often challenged by vast, high-dimensional datasets prevalent today. This chapter introduces a counterfactual-based feature selection algorithm that incorporates counterfactual reasoning to analyze and evaluate features. This innovative approach not only integrates causal analysis into the computation process but also enhances the selection effectiveness of the feature subset. The proposed algorithm includes submodular properties, allowing it to be optimized using greedy techniques, thereby significantly boosting computational efficiency. Experimental results confirm the efficacy of the algorithm, demonstrating its potential to improve feature selection outcomes in complex data environments.

articleTitle: Cable Load Characteristic Detection and Fault Diagnosis Based on BP Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: This study has successfully developed a cable load characteristic detection and fault diagnosis model based on BP neural network. The model utilizes deep learning technology to accurately detect the resistance, capacitance, and inductance parameters of cables without relying on specialized equipment such as network analyzers or impedance analyzers. By combining high-precision impedance measurement technology with neural networks, precise detection of cable parameters and diagnosis of potential faults are achieved. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in the accuracy of fault detection, processing speed, and adaptability of the model, providing new technical means for the maintenance of power systems and communication networks. It also opens up new pathways for the further development of deep learning technology in industrial applications.

articleTitle: A Clustering Method Based on K-Means and Motion Similarity in Vehicle Ad Hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Vehicle ad hoc network (VANET) have high-speed mobility, reliability and scalability, which can reduce and avoid traffic accidents according to the obtained vehicle and road information. A VANET clustering algorithm (KMSC) combining K-Means and motion similarity is proposed to solve the problem of unstable and even interrupted data transmission between VANETs due to high-speed vehicle movement and variable topology. Using elbow method, the clustering number of K-Means algorithm is no longer randomly selected, which makes the cluster convergence better. The vehicles are then assigned to the cluster based on their kinematic similarity as a measure instead of the distance parameter in the K-Means algorithm. Finally, cluster heads are selected by weight function according to kinematic similarity, node degree and average link duration ratio. The results of joint simulation using SUMO and NS3 platforms show that the KMSC algorithm has smaller end-to-end delay and larger vehicle communication throughput, which ensures the stability of inter-vehicle communication under high mobility.

articleTitle: Research on Prediction Model Based on Improved LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In this study, a prediction model based on improved Long Short-term memory Network (LSTM) is developed to improve the accuracy of time series data analysis. The model is particularly suitable for areas that require analysis and prediction of time series data, such as financial markets, weather forecasts, energy consumption, etc. It takes into account many factors such as traffic flow, meteorological conditions and historical data, and verifies and optimizes the simulation image data set. The experimental results show that the improved LSTM model has excellent performance in predicting traffic situation, especially when dealing with problems with obvious time characteristics. This model is not only suitable for traffic flow forecasting and management, but also provides new theoretical insights and practical tools for urban traffic management, and provides an important reference for researchers who study traffic forecasting technology. It is also useful in areas where similar data sets can be acquired or generated, and where traffic situation analysis is required. The excellent performance of the model is of great significance to the decision-makers and researchers who pay attention to the development trend of future traffic forecasting technology, indicating the possible far-reaching impact on the development of future traffic forecasting technology.

articleTitle: An Empirical Investigation into Complex Fake News Detection Using the Multinomial Naïve Bayes Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In recent academic discourse, the escalation of counterfeit news dissemination via social media platforms has been identified as a burgeoning concern. Conventional, labor-intensive screening practices are proving inadequate in curtailing the rapid proliferation of such false information, underscoring the necessity for the deployment of automated, machine learning-based classification systems. This study focuses on the application of the Multinomial Naïve Bayes (NB) algorithm, grounded in Bayes Theorem, notable for its minimal computational demand, reduced energy requirements, and user-friendliness. Utilizing data primarily from the years 2016 and 2017, the research employs this algorithm to develop a model, subsequently achieving a classification precision of 95%. Prior to model training, data preprocessing was conducted to distill the essential elements of each dataset. The model's efficacy was assessed using conventional metrics, including precision, recall, and the F1-score. In addition, the Support Vector Classifier (SVC) was employed as a comparative benchmark. Despite its relative simplicity compared to the SVC, the NB algorithm demonstrated commensurate performance. Further, the research delved into the distinct attributes of counterfeit news, observing a higher prevalence of imagery usage in false reports, while genuine news more frequently cited sources for information. In summary, this paper elucidates the capabilities and constraints of the Multinomial Naïve Bayes algorithm in the context of fake news classification, underscoring its potential utility in this domain.

articleTitle: Research on Anomaly Detection Methodology Combining Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: With the development of big data and artificial intelligence technologies, the importance of anomaly detection in data analysis is becoming increasingly prominent. In this study, we propose a novel detection method called SemantEdge Detection (SED), which combines large language models with unsupervised anomaly detection algorithms, aiming to improve detection performance at semantic boundaries. Four different types of unsupervised algorithms, namely iForest, HBOS, KNN, and LODA, are applied on the CCF dataset, combined with the semantic understanding ability of large language models, to experimentally verify the effectiveness of anomaly detection at boundary situations. The results demonstrate that this method effectively enhances the detection performance of unsupervised algorithms near boundary values. This study not only provides new research ideas for unsupervised anomaly detection techniques but also offers empirical evidence for the application of large language models in the field of anomaly detection.

articleTitle: Cable Lines Detection of Road Charging Piles Using Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved YOLOv8 network model to address the problem of randomly placed charging cables at roadside charging stations in recent years. In the backbone C2f module, the original convolution are replaced with SCConv (Spatial and Channel reconstruction Convolution) to form the new C2f_ScConv module, effectively reducing feature redundancy and enhancing feature representation capability. Additionally, the BiFormer attention mechanism is integrated into the head structure to focus on the subtle attributes of charging cables in complex environments, thereby enhancing network performance. Finally, the pyramid pooling module is improved by replacing SPPF with SimSPPF. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to the original YOLOv8n model, this improved algorithm shows a 9.5% improvement in mAP50 and a 4.4% improvement in mAP50-95, highlighting the effectiveness of this enhanced algorithm in accurately and quickly identifying and locating the cables of road charging piles.

Author Keywords: Detection of the cables of road charging piles

articleTitle: A Discriminative Tracking Algorithm Based on Multi-Feature Fusion Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: With the rise of embedded platforms, offline application of visual tracking technology directly on terminal platforms will become a popular remote sensing technology in the future. The current development directions usually focus on improving accuracy. Without the GPU platform, the real-time performance of the algorithm will significantly degrade. We propose a discriminative tracking method based on a multi-feature fusion mechanism, following the basic framework of correlation filter trackers. The innovation lies in two aspects: Firstly, unlike conventional direct feature fusion, we design a feature weighting mechanism to fuse two independently trained features, namely the FHOG feature and the color histogram feature. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach is more effective in exploiting the complementarity between features. Secondly, to reduce unnecessary computations and improve the inference speed of the tracker, we design a peak discrimination strategy based on average peak correlation energy to manage the scale adaptation mechanism and feature model updates. Considering our tracker needs to track targets over long distances in the air, all experiments are conducted using the UAV123 dataset as the test set. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model can be deployed on small embedded systems without neural network inference capabilities, ensuring both tracking accuracy and real-time performance.

articleTitle: A Multi-Granularity and Multi-Dimensional Code Knowledge Graph Construction Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Traditional code knowledge graphs have problems such as broad and complex knowledge coverage, incomplete code granularity, insufficient semantic richness in code relationships, and difficulty in comprehension. To address these challenges, a method for constructing a multi-granularity and multidimensional code knowledge graph was proposed. Firstly, a code knowledge graph ontology model was designed, capable of describing various granularity levels of code entities in the source code and multiple relationship dimensions between entities. Leveraging this ontology model, a methodology for constructing the code knowledge graph through knowledge extraction, fusion, and reasoning was proposed, with examples illustrating its multi-granularity and multidimensional characteristics. A prototype system capable of generating a code knowledge graph for project source code was implemented, and its application value was demonstrated using test case optimization as an example. The experimental results show that using multi-granularity and multidimensional code knowledge in the code knowledge graph can more effectively analyze the scope of code changes and help optimize test cases.

articleTitle: Research on Personalized Remote Operation and Maintenance Method of Pumped Storage Power Plant Group Security Protection System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: This study presents a personalized remote operation and maintenance (O&M) method for the security protection system in pumped storage power station groups, focusing on specialized network security and topology within the power monitoring system. The approach involves constructing a comprehensive monitoring platform, integrating management centers, emergency systems, control devices, and two-factor authentication for a production domain-specific O&M application. Key innovations include developing a primary station platform tailored to the power monitoring system's needs, incorporating advanced three-layer switches for robust network communication between the security O&M zone and plant control systems. Additionally, the research introduces a personalized remote O&M control model, enhancing the security network's effectiveness in protecting each plant's business network and ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements.

articleTitle: Travel Time Prediction Based on Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: With the continuous growth in the number of automobiles, the pressure on road traffic is constantly increasing, and the public's demand for convenient transportation is also steadily rising. However, existing research on travel time prediction has deficiencies in handling both route and global information. To address this issue, the paper proposes a new method for travel time prediction called Travel Time Prediction based on Transformer (TTPT). TTPT utilizes the multi-head attention mechanism of the Transformer model to facilitate information interactions among road segments. Additionally, to capture the temporal information of routes, we introduce Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Furthermore, we employ an improved wide and deep neural network to handle global information. Finally, we merge the outputs of these modules to comprehensively consider various information and jointly predict travel time. Through experiments on datasets from Chengdu and Shenzhen, the effectiveness of TTPT is confirmed, which also provides new insights for improving accuracy of travel time prediction.

articleTitle: BCF-YOLO: A Real-Time Detection Algorithm for Small Targets in Remote Sensing Images Based on Regional Information Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In order to solve the dilemma of detecting small targets in remote sensing images, this paper proposes a remote sensing image small target detection algorithm BCF-YOLO based on regional information fusion and multiple attention mechanisms based on YOLO v5. First, we propose a BAT module (interactive regional attention module) in the backbone, which fuses spatial and channel information in a parallel interactive way, and adopts a two-layer routing dynamic sparse attention to realize a more flexible and content-aware target detection algorithm. sparse attention to realize more flexible computational allocation with content-awareness. Second, the CF module (region-aware, information fusion module) is proposed in the feature fusion stage to perform feature fusion with reuse of feature information and close attention to the contextual information of key targets. Finally, an additional small target detection head is added and Wise IoU is introduced, while the C3 module is improved to ensure real-time monitoring with lower computational complexity and to improve the practicality of the whole detection model. The experimental results show that the recognition rate of mAP0.5:0.95 on the VisDrone2019 dataset is improved from 31.5% to 34.9% compared with YOLO v5s. Compared with other target detection algorithms, BCF-YOLO shows superior performance in small target detection on remote sensing images.

articleTitle: Video Super-Resolution with Recurrent High and Low-Frequency Information Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: The utilization of spatiotemporal complementary information of video is essential for video super-resolution (VSR). However, most VSR methods propagate the time sequence information among video frames through the initial feature, ignoring the entanglement of high and low-frequency components, which limits the performance of VSR. To address these issues, we introduce a novel recurrent propagation framework: VSR with recurrent high and low-frequency information propagation (RHLVR). Specifically, we propose a frequency decomposition module (FDM) to decompose the video sequence into high and low-frequency components, so that the network can obtain greater adaptability. In order to achieve the exploitation of high and low frequency complementary information of video sequence, a recurrent high and low-frequency information propagation unit (RHLP) is proposed to model the high and low-frequency information of the input video sequence. We perform ablation studies to confirm our designs and compare the proposed RHLVR with recent advanced VSR methods. Experimental results prove that RHLVR achieves state-of-the-art VSR performance.

articleTitle: Greenhouse Tomato Detection Based on CU-SSD
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: To improve the detection accuracy of the SSD model for small tomatoes, we proposed a new model called Continuous Up-sampling SSD (CU-SSD). This model incorporates a Conv3_3 feature layer to enhance the resolution of the features. Additionally, we have introduced a feature pyramid fusion method to improve the ability to extract features. Furthermore, we replaced the commonly used rectangular priori boxes with circular bounding boxes to improve prediction box regression. The comparison experiment demonstrates that our Circle CU-SSD model exhibits superior detection capability, achieving the greatest mean average precision (mAP) of 98.88%. The CU-SSD model enhances the mAP of the SSD and FSSD models by 22.1% and 33.1%, respectively. Furthermore, it exhibits a significant advantage over alternative models, with a 33.3% and 6.2% increase in mAP when compared to YOLOv3 and YOLOv4, respectively. Due to its smaller model size compared to YOLOv3 and YOLOv4, it achieves this improvement in mAP while maintaining a greater detection speed. Replacing rectangular boxes with circular priori-bounding boxes results in a 2.4% improvement in mAP.

articleTitle: Momentum Prediction Method Based on LSTM and LightGBM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on momentum prediction using a combination of LSTM and LightGBM models. The research utilizes a detailed dataset from the 2023 Wimbledon Championships, covering 1701 matches, to create a momentum prediction framework that incorporates various statistical data points such as serve speeds and match outcomes. The methodology includes data correction steps for misrecorded scores and speeds, followed by the application of LSTM for analyzing sequential data dependencies and LightGBM for enhancing predictive accuracy through decision tree algorithms. The paper delves into feature engineering, adjusting input variables to better reflect match dynamics, and employs a sensitivity analysis to optimize model parameters. Results indicate that the combined model effectively predicts turning points in matches, providing insights into player performance dynamics. The study advances understanding of momentum factors in tennis, highlighting the potential of machine learning in sports analytics.

articleTitle: Chinese Aspect-Level Sentiment Analysis Based on Graph Convolutional Networks with Syntactic Distance
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Aspect-level sentiment analysis tasks aimed at identifying the sentiment polarity of multiple specific aspects of a sentence. Currently most researches based on syntactic analysis have ignored the effect of different relationship types in the dependency tree to the classification results, and most of them are unable to distinguish the importance of node features to the target aspect items. To address these problems, we propose a graph convolutional network model (RD-GCN) that combines relational types and syntactic distances, where the model mainly consists of a Dependency Graph Convolutional Network (DepGCN), a Syntactic Distance Graph Convolutional Network (DisGCN), and an Affine Interaction Module. The DepGCN imports relationship type and dependency probability matrix in the feature transfer process so as to abundantly extract the structural information between the nodes; The DisGCN obtains the importance scores of each word in the sentence according to the syntactic distance matrix from the dependency tree, and setting the distance thresholds to reduce the weight proportion of the long-distance features. The RD-GCN model firstly uses the BiLSTM network as an embedding layer to obtain the initial vectors of the text, then inputs them into two different graph convolutional networks with different syntactic analyses to extract the node features respectively, finally, the affine interaction layer is used as a bridge to make the two different node features interactively learning, to improve the efficiency of the model. The experimental results show that this model on the NLP&CC2012 Chinese dataset improves the Acc and F1 values to 84.36% and 82.58% compared with the ATAE-LSTM and BiGCN comparison models. The Acc and F1 values on the two Chinese datasets of SemEval-2016 task 5 reached 83.60%, 71.99%, and 84.62%, 72.71%, respectively.

articleTitle: Cross-Camera Multi-Target Identity Association Based on Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: The current cross-camera multi-person identity association method is limited to pairwise association between cameras, lacking multi-view collaborative processing, which restricts its application in complex surveillance networks. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a cross-camera multi-target association method based on graph neural networks. It constructs a global graph structure integrating views from all cameras, extracts personnel features using a ResNet-50 network, and updates graph information through message passing and aggregation. Connectivity component constraints are introduced to optimize the graph structure and achieve accurate personnel identity association. The model is trained on the EPFL pedestrian dataset and compared with recent multi-objective association methods. The results show that the method proposed in this paper, with its ARI, AMI, and V-measure, outperforms typical methods such as Geometric, and its performance is substantially improved.

articleTitle: Keyword-Based Feedback for Interactive Document Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Document classification offers a concise comprehension of document content, which is crucial for document organization and management. However, practical scenarios pose challenges due to limited annotated data and dynamic changes in document categories. To address this, we propose an interactive document classification framework based on keyword-based feedback, which operates with minimal input-just the documents to be classified and the number of categories. We initially employ unsupervised clustering method to categorize the unlabeled documents, followed by a refine process to generate the pseudo labels for documents. Then a BERT classifier is established. In order to enhance the classifier's performance, we introduce a keyword-based interaction process. Based on the classification results from the BERT classifier, we generate representative keyword explanations. Since these keywords can identify the most significant features or characteristics within each category, returning them to users for interaction aids in their better comprehension of the current classification. We also implement user-friendly operations for result modification, promoting efficient user engagement in classifier refinement. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrated that our framework significantly improves classifier accuracy when compared to methods lacking feedback. Additionally, in comparison to approaches relying on document feedback, our framework achieves the same level of accuracy with far fewer feedback iterations.

articleTitle: Feature Enhancement and Offset Learning for Multi-Stage Human Pose Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Most of the existing studies have focused on human pose estimation at high resolution; however, research on low-resolution scenes has not yet received extensive attention. The quantization error associated with human pose estimation based on heat map regression increases as the resolution of the detected image decreases, thus seriously affecting the model's detection accuracy. Moreover, the low-resolution image itself loses much of the position information, thus increasing the difficulty of key point localization. Detection at low resolution has important applications in real-world environments and represents an urgent problem to be solved. In this paper, we propose a feature-enhanced offset learning model for human pose estimation based on the high-resolution network HRNet, effectively addressing the problem of quantization error arising from Gaussian heatmap encoding of key point location and addressing the problem of losing detailed information in low-resolution images. The model contains a multi-stage network that gradually obtains lower resolution features while maintaining the existing resolution features and improves the feature extraction capability of the backbone model by fusing different scale features. The extracted information can be enriched with positional information, semantic information, and channel context information by the feature enhancement module, thereby alleviating the problem of missing details due to the low-resolution images. This enhanced information is very important for the subsequent prediction of key points. The offset vector field-based model is used to find out the highest response point position of the heat map and take this position as a rough estimation. Subsequently, it regresses the heat map according to the offset vector to get the offset vector of the corresponding position. Finally, the final position prediction is obtained from the combination of the rough key point position and the offset vector, significantly mitigating the effect of quantization error.

articleTitle: EAM: A Vulnerability Exploitability Analysis Model Based on Program Variable Semantics
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Exploitability analysis is a crucial aspect to determine the threaten of memory corruption vulnerabilities. Previous work has attempted to assess the exploitability of vulnerabilities from various perspectives, including expert scoring, vulnerability capability detection, and fuzz testing to search for exploitable states. However, these methods have shortcomings in both accuracy and efficiency. In this paper, we present EAM, a novel vulnerability exploitability analysis model grounded in program variable semantics. Our approach entails modeling the exploitation process as a flow of exception data, moving alongside critical variables, towards an exploitable state. EAM initially constructs a knowledge graph to represent the program variable semantics by identifying such critical variables and their relationship. Subsequently, by adhering to predetermined inference rules representing exploitation techniques, EAM navigates the knowledge graph to derive exploitability analysis results, highlighting highly exploitable paths. We evaluate the effectiveness of the model through 9 vulnerabilities. The evaluation results show that EAM can correctly obtain the final exploitability result and their corresponding exploitation capabilities, including read, write, execute, and privilege escalation.

articleTitle: Joint Tracking of Delay and Frequency Offset for DSSS Systems Based on Frequency Domain Parametric Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a joint delay and frequency offset tracking scheme for solving the high-performance delay and frequency tracking problem of direct sequence spread spectrum (DSSS) systems. First, we obtain the frequency domain parametric model of the received signal by delay and frequency offset compensation and frequency domain correlation, realize the parametric model dimensionality reduction by integrate and dump in frequency domain, and after that, we obtain the joint estimation of the delay error and the frequency offset error using the rooting method, and finally realize the joint tracking of the delay and the frequency offset by a feedback loop. The proposed scheme has better delay tracking performance and constant frequency offset tracking performance with limited computational complexity increase compared with the traditional dual-loop scheme based on delay-locked and frequency-locked loops. Simulation results show the advantage of the proposed scheme in terms of tracking performance and the difference in computational complexity compared to the dual-loop scheme.

articleTitle: Optimization Study of Neural Network Mutation Testing Data Based on Set Base Evolutionary Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of inefficient test data generation and poor data quality in neural network testing, a test data generation method based on the weak mutation criterion is proposed. The mutation branch is constructed with mutation testing generated mutations, the branch is integrated into the original program, the test data is used as a decision variable, and the set base evolutionary algorithm is used to optimize the test data generation, which transforms the mutation testing data generation problem into an evolutionary optimization problem. In this problem model, this paper adopts a set base evolutionary algorithm optimization method to solve the problem and design the objective function and evolutionary strategy to generate test data with high variance scores so that it can obtain the maximum neuron coverage. Comparison experiments with existing neural network data generation show that the neural network mutation testing data optimization technique based on set base evolutionary algorithm can improve the neuron coverage under multiple granularities.

articleTitle: Research on Kiwi Surface Defect Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv7-Tiny
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
