abstract: In order to solve the problems of low precision and slow speed of kiwifruit defect detection in agricultural production line, an improved target detection algorithm GC-yolov7-tiny based on Yolov7-tiny is proposed in this paper, to detect the defect of kiwifruit on the production line in real time. Firstly, the data enhancement method is used to enrich the dataset by enhancing transformations and other operations on the collected dataset to improve the generalization ability of the model. Secondly, in the Backbone part of the model, the attention mechanism CBAM has been integrated into the MP module, resulting in the MP-CBAM structure. This innovation significantly enhances the model's feature extraction capabilities, leading to a notable improvement in detection efficiency. The optimized C3-Ghost lightweight network structure has been adopted to substitute certain ELAN modules within the backbone network. This modification effectively reduces model parameters while enhancing the detection rate. Finally, In the original network, the CIOU_Loss function has been substituted with SIOU_Loss in order to enhance both the convergence rate of the model and its detection efficiency. According to the experimental results, the defect detection mAP value of the proposed algorithm reaches 93%, and the model size is 8.5M. Compared with the original model, the mAP value increases by 0.9%, and the model size decreases by 3.8M. The proposed algorithm not only ensures a certain detection accuracy, but also reduces the size of the network model to meet the needs of real-time detection.

articleTitle: A Highly Efficient and Lightweight Graph Unlearning Method with Balanced Graph Partitioning and Adaptive Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs), designed specifically for handling graph-structured data, have been widely applied in many domains involving such data. As public awareness of privacy grows, data privacy protection is increasingly emphasized, and related regulations are continually being introduced and refined. The right to be forgotten, closely related to data privacy protection, empowers data subjects to demand data controllers delete data pertaining to them, and machine unlearning aims to address the implementation of this right in the field of machine learning. The unique characteristics of GNNs bring challenges to the corresponding machine unlearning research, for example, traditional machine unlearning algorithms are difficult to directly transfer. Moreover, for some larger-scale graphs, methods purely based on graph partitioning struggle to achieve a good balance between sub-model performance and unlearning efficiency. To address these issues, this paper presents GraphRemover, an highly efficient and lightweight graph unlearning method based on balanced graph partitioning and adaptive aggregation. Comprising three main components-balanced graph partitioning, efficient submodel training, and adaptive submodel aggregation-GraphRemover's effectiveness is demonstrated through experiments on five da-tasets, evaluating both unlearning efficiency and model utility.

articleTitle: Multi-Beam Detection Geometric Model Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: This paper develops a geometric model for multi-beam detection in seabed mapping, emphasizing the application of a genetic algorithm to optimize the layout of survey lines. Focused on addressing the challenges associated with acoustic signal projection over sloped seabeds, the study introduces novel methods for determining overlap rates, depth of seawater, and coverage width under diverse terrain conditions. It establishes a unique multi-beam space seabed coordinate system to precisely model and analyze the seafloor's geometry, facilitating the accurate mapping of marine terrains. Through the innovative use of genetic algorithms, the research optimizes the arrangement of survey lines, ensuring thorough coverage and appropriate overlap rates for effective seabed exploration. This approach not only advances the technical methodologies in marine geodesy but also broadens the scope for future applications in marine exploration and environmental monitoring, marking a significant step forward in the use of computational algorithms for enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of seabed mapping.

articleTitle: Using Mixed Wavefront for Accelerating Convolutional Neural Network Parallelization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Intra- and interoperator parallelism optimizations are the common methods to accelerate convolutional neural network (CNN) inference. Given the significant improvement in GPU performance, it is now unfeasible to achieve adequate resource utilization by exploiting intra-operator parallelism. To harness the advantages resulting from enhancements in hardware performance, inter-operator scheduling has emerged. The current inter-operator scheduler, which requires several hours to search for an appropriate schedule, greatly hampers the speed of CNN development cycles. In this paper, inter-operator scheduling is deeply investigated, and Mixed Wavefront (MW), a novel inter-operator scheduler under the guidance of runtime is proposed. The MW method may rapidly identify an appropriate collection of inter-operator schedules using a greedy scheduling strategy. Additionally, the scheduler runtime can choose a highly optimized schedule via on-board verification. Experimental results demonstrate that MW surpasses widely-used deep learning frameworks (such as TensorFlow) by a factor of up to 2.11×, Furthermore, it surpasses TensorRT, a high-performance inference library developed by NVIDIA, by a margin of up to 1.50×. The optimization cost of MW is much lower than that of IOS and TVM, with a difference of two and four orders of magnitude, respectively.

articleTitle: Named Entity Recognition Nesting Based on Synergy Between Two Feature Streams
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: To tackle the challenge of inefficient feature extraction post-text encoding, we introduce a nested model for named entity recognition, leveraging the synergy of two distinct feature streams. This model operates by embedding sentences at both word and character levels, leveraging a neural network Bi-LSTM for contextual information acquisition. Subsequently, the resultant vectors are fed into a module for low-level and high-level feature complementarity. The model further includes modules for entity word recognition and fine-grained division, enabling the extraction of internal entities within the entity word interval. Experimental findings underscore a substantial enhancement in feature extraction efficacy compared to conventional models.

Author Keywords: Mutual Enhancement of Dual Flow Characteristics

articleTitle: A Covert Spoofing Method for Trajectory Controlling of UAV
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Black flights of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) have occurred frequently in recent years, seriously endangering national defense and public safety. UAV mainly uses GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System)/INS (Inertial Navigation System) integrated system for position and navigation. Due to the weak power and open structure of GNSS signals, it is possible to counter UAV through GNSS spoofing. This article proposes a satellite navigation spoofing algorithm for trajectory controlling of UAV. Through simulation analysis, it has been proven that the proposed spoofing method can make the target UAV deviate from the original trajectory and track the spoofing trajectory, and the estimated trajectory of the integrated navigation filter still tracks the original reference trajectory, achieving the goal of covert spoofing. In addition, in order to prevent UAV tracking loop from losing lock during the spoofing process, this article also explores the impact of radar detection accuracy on concealment. Simulation analysis shows that under high-precision radar detection conditions, the spoofing algorithm can control UAVtracking spoofing trajectory more accurately.

articleTitle: A Joint-Layer Approach for Campus Network Topology Discovery
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Campus network is the cornerstone of information infrastructure for enterprises and organizations. Rapidly, reliably and precisely discovering its topology is the basis for security management. Given the shortcomings of existing network topology discovery techniques, especially multi-protocol methods, this paper leverages both the link layer, network layer and application layer protocols, and proposes a joint-layer approach that fuses the fragment information of SNMP, ICMP, LLDP and ARP for topology discovery. This approach is implemented and verified through typical star-shaped and ring-shaped network topology simulation experiments. In contrast with existing multi-protocol methods, it can effectively restore the complete topological information even with the incomplete SNMP support from adjacent devices, proving its robustness and flexibility.

articleTitle: Personalized Recommendation Algorithm in AI-Assisted Learning System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, AI-assisted learning systems have become an important tool in the field of education. However, when providing personalized learning resources to users, existing recommendation algorithms still face many challenges. The explosive growth of the number of Internet users has led to a significant increase in the number of daily web searches and the amount of information available on the portal. This means that it becomes even more difficult for users to search or discover things that interest them in a large amount of data. Personalized recommendation systems have then emerged as an important tool to help users overcome information barriers, and therefore have been applied by major websites. The existing personalized recommendation systems have problems such as inaccurate capture of user preferences, excessive requirements for dialogue rounds, and inappropriate recommendation timing. In response to these issues, this study combines graph convolutional networks to design a hybrid model, which helps AI-assisted learning systems make more appropriate and reasonable decision actions. This system can more comprehensively mine the real-time preferences of users. Finally, through experimental comparison, the resource recommendation accuracy of the algorithm in this study performed the best, reaching as high as 0.9914. Its recall ratio reached 0.9421, and the F1 score reached 0.8823. The excellent performance was also reflected in practical applications, which could prove that the system in this study has higher application value compared to other popular systems.

articleTitle: Simulation of Ultrashort Wave Communication Scenario Based on Digital Twin Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Ultrashort wave communication is playing an increasingly important role in the field of wireless communication guarantee. Digital twin has become a new choice to solve complex system problems with its full use of data resources and good interaction ability with physical entities. To better play to the potential of ultrashort wave communication equipment, effectively improve the efficiency of ultrashort wave communication network, design ultrashort wave communication scenario simulation scheme, based on the digital twin technology synchronization and feedback of simulation scenario, this paper from the four elements of digital twin design simulation, the network layer, data link layer and physical layer modeling simulation, three layers of simulation interdependence, jointly ensure the accuracy of ultrashort wave communication equipment model, considering the realistic factors, with the aid of ultrashort wave network modeling and scene simulation of communication equipment model. Call engine to realize software synchronization, using DIS distributed half physical access method to realize simulation and real synchronization for real-time feedback data transmission channel, when feedback based on data fusion spectrum measurement and simulation results combined feedback mechanism, first quantitative parameters and communication network performance index, fusion feedback to the simulation system, and then cycle, get the parameter adjustment recommended scheme, finally through experimental verification, in a specific communication environment network communication performance is optimized, packet loss rate and system delay are obviously decreased, prove the accuracy of scene simulation and the effectiveness of the feedback algorithm design.

articleTitle: A New Algorithm for Vehicle Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: As the basic function of advanced assisted driving technology or autonomous driving technology, vehicle recognition plays an important role in lane change, collision avoidance and other applications. The current vehicle recognition method has the problem of slow recognition speed and false detection caused by camera movement. In order to solve this problem, this paper improves the existing three-frame difference method. The candidate frames obtained by the three-frame difference method are then screened and identified by FAST feature extraction, and tested in a typical vehicle video data set. The test results show that the average number of targets detected by mistake per frame is reduced from 1.5 to 0.15 when the camera is rotating incorrectly, and the detection rate is also increased by 10% when the camera is not moving.

articleTitle: IOTToe: A Smart System for In/Out-Toeing Foot Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Toe-in and toe-out angles show difficulties in assessing and addressing gait abnormalities, posture issues, and joint stress, requiring sophisticated monitoring and treatment strategies in musculoskeletal health. Diagnostic and Detecting toe-in/out angles is important because of its rules and index into gait abnormalities, posture imbalances, and potential joint stress, enabling early intervention and personalized treatment to improve musculoskeletal health and prevent long-term complications. While various diagnostic methods have been developed, the diagnosis of this disease continues to rely heavily on the expertise of healthcare professionals. Researchers are actively seeking more dependable and convenient approaches to assist patients in achieving earlier diagnoses and monitoring treatment progress effectively. With the importance of this measurement, the proposed design system named IOTToe based on the Internet of Things (IOT) aims to create an effective and user-friendly tool for measuring toe-in and toe-out angles accurately and easily. A web-based interface enables real-time remote tracking of foot alignment, reducing the need for physical tests and making reports. The telemetric capabilities facilitate efficient data transmission, empowering medical professionals with valuable insights for personalized treatment and enhancing healthcare efficiency. Integration with hospital systems supports advanced research in musculoskeletal health. The obtained results show the ability of the system to help the diagnosis and treatment process.

articleTitle: Improving Intra-Urban Prediction of Regional Pedestrian Flow Using a Hybrid Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In modern urban management, the monitoring and prediction of pedestrian flow is a crucial task. The development and application of mobile terminals and positioning services have generated a large amount of pedestrian flow data, along with a massive amount of heterogeneous urban data. Accurately predicting pedestrian flow information can provide strong scientific evidence for traffic management and the formulation of public safety policies. Pedestrian flow prediction is commonly modeled as a time series forecasting problem. Currently, neural network models based on convolutional neural networks (CNN) and long short-term memory networks (LSTM) are widely applied for this task. However, there are still shortcomings in the fusion of multidimensional spatiotemporal heterogeneous data, the extraction of multiscale temporal patterns, and the modeling of cross-regional correlations. This paper proposes an improved cascaded prediction method based on the framework of CNN-LSTM, which utilizes the CNN network to extract and fuse heterogeneous features, models different time scales separately, and incorporates Gaussian functions to model the correlations between regions. The cascaded method has high scalability and outperforms all baseline models in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: Flying Ad-Hoc Network Routing Algorithm Based on Knowledge-Graph Embedding
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Flying ad-hoc network (FANET) are novel self-organizing networks that have good scalability, robustness, multifunctionality, flexibility, and low cost, making them widely applicable in both military and civilian fields. However, because of the rapid movement of FANET nodes, constant changes in network topology, and limited network resources, developing efficient routing algorithms is challenging. In this paper, we propose a FANET network-topology representation and routing strategy based on knowledge-graph embedding. We model the proposed network to represent nodes, links, and user messages with fixed-dimensional vectors. The model considers node-forwarding delays, link-transmission delays, and network resources to make routing decisions, and uses the routing results of historical messages for further optimization. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm adapts well to an expanding and dynamic network, reduces the packet-loss rate and end-to-end delay, balances the consumption of network resources, and increases the network lifecycle.

articleTitle: Infrared Thermal Image Fault Detection of Electric Motor Based on Improved VGG16 Network Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: As a core component of modern industry, electric motors are widely used in important fields such as electric power, machinery and national defense, and the fault detection of their thermal images faces problems such as diverse fault types, insufficient complex data processing capability and long training time. To address the above problems, this paper proposes a method for fault detection of infrared thermal images of electric motors based on an improved VGG16 network model. In the model construction and implementation, based on the VGG16 network model, the significant optimization of training time and accuracy is achieved by improving the structure of the latter layers of the model and introducing the migration learning strategy, as well as adding the callback function, the AdamW optimizer and the focal point loss function to the model. The experimental results show that the improved VGG16 model increases the average accuracy by 12.96%, reduces the average loss rate by about 23 times, and shortens the training time by half in infrared thermal image fault detection of induction motors. In the model performance evaluation, whether adjusting the test conditions or conventional model evaluation methods, the results reflect the superiority of the improved model in the realm of infrared thermal image anomaly identification of induction motors, which has practical application value.

articleTitle: Parameterized Water Body Twin Model Construction Research
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: With the continuous development of digital twin technology, it has been widely applied in various fields. The application of digital twin technology in the water environment is becoming a hot topic, bringing new possibilities for water quality monitoring and early warning. Digital twin models are the core elements of digital twins. Currently, existing digital twin models of water bodies are mainly implemented in a static manner, making it difficult to express the dynamic changes of water bodies, integrate with environmental factors, and achieve realistic water twin scenarios. This paper proposes the construction of water body twin models through parameterization, and by integrating environmental parameters, accurately and intuitively expresses the characteristics and dynamic changes of water bodies. This has reference significance for promoting the development of digital twin technology.

articleTitle: VulD-CodeBERT: CodeBERT-Based Vulnerability Detection Model for C/C++ Code
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Recently, deep learning techniques have received widespread attention in code vulnerability and vulnerability detection. However, there are some problems with current vulnerability detection techniques, firstly, because of the non-homogeneity of vulnerability categories and quantities, there are omission false positives and overfitting problems for vulnerabilities with a small amount of data. Second, the existing detection methods have limited ability to characterize the code, there is insufficient depth of characterization, does not contain all of its vulnerability characteristics or is interspersed with useless information. Finally, the current research does not use the powerful feature mining capability of pre-trained models and does not employ model fusion to increase the effectiveness of model vulnerability detection. To solve the above problems, this paper proposes a new deep learning based pre-trained model for code vulnerability detection tool VulD-CodeBERT. By fine-tuning CodeBERT, a code adaptation extension for pre-trained models developed by Microsoft, the CodeBERT model can solve the problem of not being able to learn the vulnerability patterns due to insufficient data, thus resulting in missed false alarms. The sequence output from the CodeBERT model are added to a BiLSTM network with an attention mechanism to mine the local key features of the vulnerabilities combined with the global features of the pooler output from the CodeBERT model to deeply mine the dependencies between the vulnerability statements and derive the probability of the existence of the vulnerability. For vulnerability types that are difficult to uncover captured features or the number of samples is not enough, a polynomial plain Bayesian classifier is used for detection, and finally the two models are combined to deeply mine the vulnerability features, thus solving the problem of difficult and small samples, and reducing the leakage rate and false alarm rate. Experimental results show that VulD-CodeBERT is more effective compared to using only sub-models such as the CodeBERT model. It performs better in side-by-side comparison with other detectors such as Devign, ReVEAL.

articleTitle: Multi-Index Decision Analysis Method Based on TOPSIS and Random Forest Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: This study introduces a comprehensive multi-index decision analysis framework integrating TOPSIS and the Random Forest model, focusing on various insurance-related models. The research primarily develops and tests three models: the InsuraClient Ecosystem Connectivity Model (ICEC), the InsuraSite Selection Analytics Model (ISSA), and the Community Building Preservation Guideline Model (CBPG). Each model is equipped to analyze different aspects of the insurance industry through statistical methods such as GM (11), ARMA, and ARIMA models to predict risk awareness, claims, and the frequency of natural disasters, respectively. The ICEC model applies multiple linear regression to forecast profits and guide insurance decisions based on client risk awareness and natural disaster data. In contrast, the ISSA model uses TOPSIS to optimize real estate development locations by considering factors like infrastructure and population growth. Lastly, the CBPG model utilizes factor analysis and Random Forest to preserve community buildings by evaluating demographic, and construction-related factors. Overall, the paper extends traditional decision analysis models by effectively combining these methodologies to tackle analytical challenges, offering new methodological advancements in data-driven environments.

articleTitle: Credit Rating Prediction Based on WOA-Cross-Validation-LightGBM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: One of the key challenges faced by banks in the context of continuous growth in customer loan demand is how to effectively execute customer credit ratings. This study introduces SMOTE to solve the problem of data imbalance and utilizes RFE_XG-Boost for feature importance assessment to screen out the key features that have a significant impact on credit ratings. Based on these selected features, the LightGBM model is used to predict customer credit ratings. To further optimize the model performance, this paper applies the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) to adjust the parameters of the LightGBM model and combines with the 5-fold cross-validation technique to enhance the model prediction accuracy. Using this method, the study significantly improves the accuracy of the model prediction. The experimental results confirm that the LightGBM model, which combines SMOTE, RFE_XGBoost feature selection and WOA, shows high accuracy and practicality in credit rating prediction. The methodology of this study provides an efficient solution for bank credit rating and lays the foundation for future research in similar areas.

articleTitle: Transformer Encoder-Decoder Mask Reconstruction in Industrial Image Anomaly Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Acquiring a substantial amount of high-quality data for industrial image detection poses significant challenges in the field of computer vision. The imbalance between normal and anomalous samples, where normal samples far outnumber anomalies, complicates the training of traditional supervised detection methods, limiting their ability to exhibit robust detection performance on industrial image datasets. Unsupervised anomaly detection methods based on image reconstruction train exclusively on normal samples. These methods employ encoders and decoders to map and reconstruct images, assessing deviations from the distribution by evaluating unseen instances of both normal and anomalous cases. We propose a method for anomaly localization in industrial images using Transformer Encoder-Decoder Mask Reconstruction. The self-attention mechanism of the Transformer enables better attention to different positions within the entire input image in both the encoder and decoder, capturing long-range dependencies in the image and more accurately learning crucial features. Additionally, to train a stable and efficient image reconstruction network, we introduce a block-wise reconstruction approach involving masking the input images. To validate the algorithm's generality in industrial images, experiments are conducted on the MVTecAD and a custom crankshaft bearing datasets. Experimental results demonstrate the algorithm's excellent detection performance, surpassing previous state-of-the-art methods and confirming its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Deep Analysis Model of ECG Signals Combining Channel Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: This study introduces a Multi-Scale Attention ResNet Model for the assisted diagnosis of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. Utilizing deep learning techniques, the model enhances neural networks via a residual learning framework to prevent gradient vanishing, thus improving classification accuracy and recognition rates. Specifically tailored for 12-lead ECG data, the model employs multi-scale convolution and channel attention mechanisms to accurately analyze cardiac data. Capable of identifying common cardiac conditions as well as handling complex or ambiguous cases, the model also integrates patient information to enhance classification performance. Serving as an efficient tool for managing extensive data in clinical diagnostics, this model is anticipated to become a pivotal technology in clinical diagnostics and telemedicine.

articleTitle: A Method for Identifying Radio Frequency Interference Sources Based on Near-field Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Currently, conventional single-probe sensor technology for wireless radio frequency near-field measurements suffers from inefficiencies and low accuracy. This study introduces a design that employs a multi-probe array to conduct radio frequency near-field signal assessments. By adjusting the measurement distances within the probe array, it enables detailed analysis of the radiation characteristics in the RF signal's near field. The significant time benefits inherent in array testing greatly enhance the measurement efficiency, and after compensating for probe effects, a high level of precision can be achieved. The research specifically focuses on the identification and differentiation of near-field interference sources in proximity to signal emitters, particularly addressing co-channel and inter-channel interference scenarios. Initially, under conditions of a single-frequency interference source, the work systematically investigates the influence pattern of distance variables on the degree of interference experienced by the signal source. Through experimental measurements, a model is established to represent the variation of interference field strength with increasing or decreasing distance in a single-frequency near-field environment. This model serves as a basis for discerning and categorizing interference sources into two distinct types: co-frequency and inter-frequency. Building upon this foundational research, further investigation is conducted into situations where multiple co-frequency or inter-frequency interference sources are concurrently present. Experimental results confirm that by comparing and contrasting the distance-dependent field strength curves constructed for both co-frequency and inter-frequency interference sources, precise discrimination and identification of various co-frequency and inter-frequency interference sources can be successfully accomplished.

articleTitle: A High-Speed Data Acquisition and Control System Based on LabVIEW for Long-Pulse Experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: It is well known that energy has become one of the essential factors for the development of human civilization. As a new type of energy source, fusion energy is considered to be the most promising and effective way to solve future energy problems. With the continuous research in this field, the current types of pulse experiments have gradually developed into long-pulse experiment operation mode. This paper designs a data acquisition and control system (DACS) in order to meet the requirements of high-speed data acquisition and efficient storage in the context of long-pulse experiments. This system designs a new data transmission and storage management mode to enable the interaction between LabVIEW and MDSplus, making it suitable for multi-channel high-speed data acquisition experiments in long-pulse mode. Besides, DACS uses MDSip and HTTP network communication protocols to transmit control signals and experimental data. As for human-machine interaction, it adopts a combination of local and remote interactions to satisfy the requirements of different situations. It also devises a suitable algorithm to solve the concurrent processing problem of double platforms. The design of this system can accomplish the tasks of monitoring and control as well as real-time processing and storage of experimental data in long-pulse experiments, improving the overall level of automation of the system.

articleTitle: Text Similarity Calculation Model Based on Semantic Information and Syntactic Structure Fusion Weighting
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of traditional text similarity calculation methods that do not fully use the different importance of different parts of the text and ignore the syntactic structure information, this paper proposes a text similarity calculation model based on semantic information and syntactic structure fusion weighting (SSFW). Firstly, a semantic similarity calculation model based on multiple granularity information interactions is designed to accurately extract interaction information and highlight the importance of different granularities. Then, a text similarity calculation model based on Tree-GRU is proposed to perform syntactic structure similarity calculation on the basis of shallow syntactic trees. Finally, the calculation results of semantic similarity and structural similarity are linearly weighted to obtain the text similarity calculation results. The experimental results show that the SSFW model can improve the accuracy and recall rate, which is better than other text similarity calculation methods and more suitable to deal with complex long texts.

articleTitle: A Study of Fusion Strategies for Self-Attention Enhanced Convolutional Neural Networks in Short Text Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the application of self-attention enhanced convolutional neural network in short text classification and introduce a dynamic fusion strategy. Given the sparseness and semantic ambiguity of short text, traditional methods are difficult to handle effectively. In this paper, the global comprehension ability of the model is improved by combining the CNN with the self-attention mechanism, using the CNN to capture local features and highlighting key semantic information through the self-attention mechanism. A dynamic fusion strategy is adopted to dynamically adjust the fusion degree of CNN and self-attention mechanism to further improve the classification performance. Experimental results show that the fusion model outperforms traditional methods in accuracy, recall and F1 score on datasets such as Twitter sentiment analysis, IMDB movie reviews and Yelp restaurant reviews, validating the effectiveness of the dynamic fusion strategy.

articleTitle: Lightweight Motorcycle Helmet Detection Based on Improved YOLOv7-Tiny
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In response to the current issues of detection models not effectively balancing accuracy and speed, and failing to screen out helmeted pedestrians in traffic environments, we propose a helmet detection model based on an improved YOLOv7-Tiny architecture. Firstly, we introduce the Gather-and-Distribute mechanism in the model's neck to enhance the fusion of shallow features and improve the semantic information of small target helmets. Additionally, by integrating Deformable Convolution v4 (DCNv4) with the CBL module in the backbone network, we enhance the model's ability to extract features from irregular shapes in the feature map, improving its detection capability for occluded and overlapping targets. Furthermore, for small target detection, we incorporate the idea of a shape-IOU loss function into the Normalized Wasserstein Distance, replacing the CIOU loss function in the model. Both CBL-Dcnv and GD modules improve model accuracy without significantly increasing model weight. This ensures a balance between detection accuracy and speed. Finally, we propose a helmet screening strategy to exclude non-riders wearing helmets and accurately detect riders wearing helmets. Experimental results show that the improved model increases the mean Average Precision (mAP) value by eight percentage points while maintaining detection speed within lightweight standards.

articleTitle: Smart Firefighting Early Warning and Evacuation System Based on Edge Computing with Led Dynamic Indicator Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: The current standard practice for building fire safety relies heavily on regular lighting, emergency lighting, and smoke sensors. The management and control centers for these systems are typically separate and independent, resulting in a bulky and expensive local control system that is difficult to use and manage. Additionally, the traditional fixed instructions in fire protection systems do not allow for adaptive planning of optimal escape routes based on the location of the fire, leading to delays in evacuation and ultimately causing significant casualties. This paper presents the design of a smart fire warning and evacuation system based on edge computing utilizing LED dynamic indication devices. The system integrates LED dot-matrix technology to create a smart indicator and emergency light with dynamic adaptive indication capabilities. Additionally, it includes temperature, humidity, and smoke sensors to monitor the building's environmental conditions. Through Mesh wireless networking, time-series sensing data is aggregated to the edge gateway, where a miniature machine learning model trained by the Edge Impluse (EI) platform performs edge computing for predicting and reasoning about fire situations. The data is then uploaded to a cloud server and forwarded to mobile users via Cat.1 communication protocol for real-time monitoring. The system also incorporates an improved ant colony algorithm for automatic execution in the cloud and allows manual commands from mobile terminals to control adaptive and dynamic indication of indicator lights and emergency lights, guiding building personnel to the safest evacuation path. System testing demonstrates a high accuracy rate of 95% for fire prediction and inference, with an average inference time of less than 1 ms. This system provides a novel approach to adaptive building fire prediction and evacuation, enhancing safety measures for orderly and secure evacuations.

articleTitle: Research on Key Technology of UAV Communication Optical Cable Line Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Based on the reality of UAV communication optical cable line patrol technology, and the application status of patrol system and operation platform, this paper systematically discusses the key problems of UAV patrol, summarizes its key technologies from three aspects of flight platform, communication link platform and ground command and control platform, and points out the technical development and design requirements and the next development trend of UAV patrol. It has certain reference value for deepening the reform of value dimension mode in the communication industry.

articleTitle: DAGNN: Deep Autoencoder-Based Graph Neural Network for Local Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Nowadays, traditional anomaly detection methods, which are known as local outlier methods, such as LOF and DBSCN, are always based on measuring distances between one sample with its neighborhoods to judge whether it is an outlier or not. Although their principles are straightforward, their performance are always good for feature-based datasets. However, there exist many such cases that a group of neighboring samples are anomalies, which are unsuitable for these methods. In this paper, a novel local anomaly detection model DAGNN is proposed, which incorporates a graph neural network to better aggregate neighbors' distance information of each sample for forming its latent representation vector, and a deep autoencoder to reconstruct this latent representation vector for eliminating noises collected from neighbors. According to results of extensive experiments implemented on multiple publicly available datasets, our model DAGNN outperforms existing baseline methods in terms of detection performance and execution speed. Additionally, these experiment results also indicate that DAGNN is more robust, particularly when the number of neighbors changes.

articleTitle: Efficient Discovery of Spouses for Causal Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: The identification of Markov Blankets (MB) plays a pivotal role in the domains of structural learning and the optimization of feature selection within Bayesian Networks (BN). Although numerous algorithms for efficient or effective MB discovery have been introduced, a persistent challenge remains the reconciliation of computational accuracy with speed. This paper introduces a novel MB discovery algorithm, Efficient Discovery of Spouses for Markov Blankets discovery (ESMB), which enhances spouses identification efficiency by narrowing the candidate set's search range during the PC discovery algorithm phase, and use the separation set to further narrow the spouses search space based on the spouse sufficiency condition before using the AND rule. We evaluate the ESMB algorithm against leading MB discovery algorithms across a suite of standard Bayesian network datasets. Our findings demonstrate that ESMB achieves a balance between execution efficiency and accuracy, rivaling the fastest MB discovery algorithms in speed while approaching the accuracy of the most emblematic MB discovery algorithms. This balance is particularly pronounced in the context of large Bayesian Networks.

articleTitle: User Identity Identification of Energy Storage Power Plant Power Monitoring Platform Supporting Dual Factor Authentication
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In order to enhance the security of the system, it is necessary to introduce a dual factor authentication mechanism, which requires additional authentication of user identity in addition to traditional usernames and passwords. This study aims to provide an identity authentication scheme that supports dual factor authentication, which can use multiple factors such as fingerprints, multiplayer authentication, tokens, etc. to increase the reliability and difficulty of authentication, ensuring that only legitimate users can access the monitoring platform. This approach provides a higher level of security and can prevent unauthorized access. And simulation experiments were conducted to confirm the feasibility of this method.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Wave Energy Optimization for FAST Active Reflector Based on Householder Optical Transformation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: The five hundred meters aperture spherical radio telescope (FAST) is a radio telescope with independent intellectual property rights in China. Electromagnetic waves are an important energy for radio telescopes. By optimizing the electromagnetic wave energy that can be received by the feed cabin, we can greatly increase the scientific value and economic benefits of FAST. In this paper, the corresponding ideal parabolic equations are determined when the feed cabin is located in the vertical illumination position and the random illumination position. This article determines the ratio of the received reflected energy in the effective area of the feed cabin to the reflected energy from the reflecting surface within 300 meters aperture while calculating the received ratio to the reference reflecting sphere, further making a comparison. As the contribution, the modeling of the study scenario is implemented using Householder's optical transformation method simulation. This paper determines the parabolic equations based on the profile of FAST. In addition, this paper models the ideal paraboloid. With constraints, the coordinate positions where each reflecting surface is located are calculated. For the calculation of the acquisition rate, we adopt the idea of utilizing the microelement method to find the receiving ratio of the feed cabin. Subsequently, the reception ratio is compared with that of the reference surface. After simulation through MATLAB coding, the reception ratio of the feed cabin can reach 32.57% and that of the reference spherical surface can reach 5.67%, which is an improvement of 5.75 times. Our method has the best performance when compared with the literature which has the same constraints and modeling assumptions.

articleTitle: Towards Understanding Rust in the Era of AI for Science at an Ecosystem Scale
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Rust is an emerging programming language that provides both memory and thread safety like Java, and runtime efficiency like C/C++, by introducing a number of novel language features such as ownership, borrowing, explicit lifetime, and unsafe. These novel features make Rust a promising safe system language to build infrastructures in AI for science, where both security and performance are indispensable. However, there are no prior empirical studies of Rust language feature usage at the ecosystem scale, and such a study is important not only for guiding future language evolution but also for identifying research opportunities and challenges. In this paper, to fill the gap, we present the first comprehensive empirical study of Rust language feature usage at the ecosystem scale, by analyzing all registered 9,683 science-related crates in the Rust community's crate registry, with a novel tool RInsight we created. The empirical results give important insights, such as: 1) the dominated language features in all crates are functional ones (66.67<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), which presents evidence that Rust is essentially a functional language pragmatically, but does NOT support the claim that “Rust is a safe dialect of C”; and 2) the unsafe feature is not used at an as high ratio as the prior study reported and is continuously dropping since 2018. We present the implications of these empirical findings and future research challenges to promote future research.

articleTitle: GNN_NEI: A Network Entity Identification Model Based on Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Network Entity Identification (NEI) is an essential issue in network security, which involves identifying various classes of entities with IP attributes on the Internet. Traditional NEI methods tend to have the disadvantage of being ineffective in the face of large-scale, complex network data; these GNN-based heterogeneous models require all nodes to have attributes. However, this is only sometimes satisfied in a network topology graph. In network topology graphs, specific entity node attributes are typically said to be missing, which leads to a decline in the accuracy of NEI task. The missing attributes can be obtained learnable by utilizing network entity features combined with graph neural networks embedded in the nodes of the graph to get a numerical vector representation of the entity nodes. And propose a graph neural network-based NEI model (GNN_NEI), including data processing, node information update and graph neural network classifier. GNN_NEI model performs an attribute aggregation update step by calculating the weights between nodes, followed by classification, and finally outputs the entity types. The GNN_NEI model has significantly improved all the indexes compared with other methods, and the identification accuracy is over 92.37%, and the highest can reach 95.42%.

articleTitle: An Container Elastic Autoscaling Strategy Based Adaptive Integrated Resource Forecast
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: The built-in elastic autoscaling strategy of Kubernetes, a container cloud orchestration and management system, balances the relationship between application service quality and cluster resource usage by regularly monitoring a single resource and comparing it with a set threshold to determine whether to scale up or down. However, the built-in strategy has the problems of incomplete evaluation of a single resource index, response delay and scaling jitter. To address the above problems, this paper uses an adaptive weighting algorithm to obtain a comprehensive prediction index based on long-range time multi-resource prediction sequences. This index is not only more comprehensive than a single index, but also measures the resource usage in the future time period, so that the adaptive comprehensive prediction index has the ability to more comprehensively measure the changes in application workload in the future time period. The experimental results show that the autoscaling strategy based on adaptive integrated resource forecast can effectively solve the problems of regulation lag and scaling jitter.

articleTitle: Pose Estimation of Multiple Domains Based on the Fusion of Multiple Deep Learning Models and Baidu API
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: To enhance the precision of pose estimation across various domains, this study introduces a method that leverages the general object recognition capabilities of the Baidu API. For an unfamiliar image, we first employ the output of the Baidu API to infer its domain, then proceed with keypoint detection using a pose estimation model pre-trained on relevant domain datasets. This approach has been validated through extensive experiments on three widely-used datasets: MPII, Animalpose, and Animalkingdom. In comparison to existing algorithms, our method reduces the number of high-performance models to be trained, thus minimizing computational demands and ensuring high scalability. Experimental findings confirm that our method is not only simpler but also more accurate.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation of Remote Sensing Images Based on Improved Deeplabv3+ Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In the context of rapid development, remote sensing imaging technology is widely used in environmental monitoring, disaster warning and other fields. As an important component of remote sensing image processing, semantic segmentation of remote sensing images is also highly valued. Traditional remote sensing image segmentation methods are mostly based on manual features and simple classifiers, but they are limited by the complexity, diversity, and scale changes of remote sensing images, making it difficult for these methods to achieve ideal results. This article proposes a method for semantic segmentation of remote sensing images based on an improved Deeplabv3+ network. Based on the Keras deep learning framework <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>, a convolutional neural network based on Deeplabv3+ <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[2] [3]</sup> is designed, and many small modifications are made to the network to improve the segmentation results. Comparative experiments were conducted between the proposed method and common semantic segmentation methods <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[4]–[5]</sup>, and the experimental results showed that the proposed method has relatively excellent mIOU and Kappa coefficients, and has excellent semantic segmentation performance, making it suitable for training on small-scale datasets. Meanwhile, due to the high bias of target categories in small-scale datasets, the classification accuracy for certain categories is relatively low. Further research is needed, such as using GAN methods to enhance segmentation accuracy.

articleTitle: FCTNet: A Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Method for Land Cover Classification Based on CNN and Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Land cover classification is vital for urban planning, environmental management, and monitoring. CNNs excel at local feature extraction but struggle with long-range dependencies. Transformers effectively model global contextual information but face challenges with local features. To address these issues, we propose FCTNet, which integrates ResNet and CSWin Transformer networks for global-local multi-scale feature fusion. CSWin Transformer captures global features, while ResNet extracts local texture and edge features, enhancing semantic information extraction. We introduce the GLIM and LCM to fuse CNN and Transformer features effectively. Additionally, the MFFD module adaptively integrates information from different levels and scales to enhance model classification accuracy. Extensive experiments are conducted on datasets from the International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (ISPRS), Vaihingen, and Homemade datasets. The results showed that the proposed FCTNet outperformed single CNN or Transformer methods, obtaining a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) score of 93.03%, which was 2.31 and 4.01% higher than DeepLab-V3+and Attention Aggregation Feature Pyramid Network (A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>FPN), respectively, which are mainstream landcover classification methods. Additionally, the proposed method exhibited a superior performance when applied to the public ISPRS Vaihighen dataset, with an mIoU score reaching 76.47%, corresponding to an improvement of 2.30 and 1.18% compared with the DeepLab-V3+and A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>FPN methods, respectively. The FCTNet model's ability to generalise on various datasets was thoroughly demonstrated.

articleTitle: Multiple Time-Periods POI Recommendation Model Based on Distributed ELM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: To solve the problems of low efficiency of algorithm execution and not fully considering the POI needs of users in different time-periods in point-of-interest (POI) recommendation. In this paper, propose a Multiple time-periods POI recommendation model MP-DELM based on distributed extreme learning machine (DELM). According to the user's different periods and different types of POI access requirements, the data set was processed in different periods; extract POI preference features: distance preference feature, personalized preference feature, popularity preference feature, and friend preference feature, in which for the friend preference feature, social friend feature and the trajectory feature are integrated for the first time, and a new trajectory friend similarity calculation method is proposed; in order to improve the efficiency of POI recommendation, improve DELM classifier. And the online sequential extreme learning machine (OS-ELM) is used to update training data in real time. Finally, we prove that the MP-DELM recommendation model can effectively improve the accuracy and efficiency of POI recommendation in the real datasets.

articleTitle: A Propagation Model Based on Benign Worm Confrontation and Monitoring in Peer-to-Peer Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In peer-to-peer (P2P) resource-sharing networks, worms spread rapidly. Currently, the technique of using benign worms against malicious worms is prone to problems such as resource burden and network congestion. Therefore, this paper proposes a new model, namely M-SIBR. First, based on the existing model (SIBR) of benign worms against malicious worms, a monitoring compartment is introduced, i.e. M. The benign infected node feeds back the information of the neighbor list according to the characteristics of the network, and adds the node with the largest infection probability in the current susceptible state to the monitoring state, to better control the spreading of the worm. Secondly, we calculate the equilibrium point and propagation threshold of the new model, and prove the local and global stability of the equilibrium point by using the Routh Hurwitz criterion and the Lyapunov function. Finally, the results of numerical simulation experiments show that the introduction of the monitoring mechanism can effectively contain the spread of the worm.

articleTitle: Text Classification for Social Governance: A Novel Strategy with Adaptive Reward Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Given the increasing need for societal governance systems to effectively address public grievances, classifying texts from public service hotlines and other governance communications has become challenging, especially for texts with complex hierarchical structures. This study explores how adaptive reward mechanisms can be applied to classify complaint texts in societal governance. We propose a novel hierarchical text classification model that overcomes the limitations of traditional methods in handling hierarchical data. We designed a hierarchical loss function that considers inter-label hierarchical relationships to enhance the model's learning of hierarchical information. Additionally, we used a simple label encoding method to reduce computational complexity and improve training efficiency. Experimental results show that our model significantly outperforms existing methods in classification accuracy, both flat and hierarchical. Furthermore, ablation studies confirmed the hierarchical loss function's crucial role in enhancing model performance. This research offers an effective strategy for classifying complex hierarchical data, significantly improving classification tasks in natural language processing.

articleTitle: A Methodology for Infilling Missing Data in Smart Power Grids Based on Correlation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: In modern urban power systems, the increase in multiple energy resources has led to greater difficulty in data acquisition, resulting in a higher random missing data rate. As a result, it has become challenging to meet the requirements for refined analysis and decision-making. To address the frequent missing data issue in the measurement and transmission processes of the distribution network in the new power system, a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network based on correlation analysis (WGAN-CA) is proposed to infill the smart power grid missing data. Real power grid data is utilized in the algorithm verification and tested in a city power grid. The results indicate that the proposed method has higher filling accuracy compared to traditional data filling methods. Therefore, in the case of continuous missing measurement data and a large amount of missing data in the new power system, integrating strongly correlated features for data filling has significant advantages in improving the integrity and availability of measurement data.

articleTitle: Passive Location Discrete Point Trace Clustering Algorithm Based on Improved DBSCAN and ACO
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Passive location scouting acquires target location information by passively receiving electromagnetic waves from the radiation source, which is more susceptible to the influence of the electromagnetic environment leading to the dispersion of the location point trace, and the acquisition of the location point feature information is relatively less. Therefore, to address the large positioning error and low feature quantity of passive location discrete traces, this paper proposes a passive location discrete point trace clustering algorithm based on improved Density Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO). In this algorithm, iterative blind DBSCAN (IB-DBSCAN) segments the multi-target discrete point traces to form two types of clusters, and the integration of clustered clusters is realized through cyclic pathfinding ACO (CP-ACO) algorithm processing to complete the clustering of passive location discrete point traces. Simulation experimental results demonstrate that the algorithm can effectively improve clustering accuracy in environments with large positioning error and high leakage rate, even in the face of multiple target passive location discrete traces with different motion characteristics.

articleTitle: A Study of Nanosecond Clock Synchronization Methods for Real-Time Transient Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Conventional nanosecond clock synchronization protocols are generally target-type or content-type, the synchronization rate is low, which leads to the increasing of the mean value difference of synchronization, so we propose to study the design of nanosecond clock synchronization method for real-time transient simulation. Combined with the actual clock synchronization requirements, we first calculate the link congestion coefficient, adopt a multilevel approach to strengthen the synchronization rate, set up a multilevel clock synchronization protocol, based on which we determine the clock source quality coefficients and construct a nanosecond clock synchronization model for real-time transient simulation, and use redundancy processing to achieve clock synchronization. The test results show that compared with the high-efficiency phase-color clock synchronization method and the cross-clock synchronization method, the mean synchronization difference of the designed transient simulation nanosecond clock synchronization method is controlled to be less than 0.5, which indicates that the designed clock synchronization method is more efficient, stable, and targeted, and the synchronization effect is significantly improved.
